correctness.rationale: Let A=V^3⊕Kz, uv=B(u,v)z, zA=0, char K odd and B nondegenerate. Every Hamiltonian derivation preserves Ann(A)=Kz, so {z,u}=β(u)z. From 0={u²,u}=B(u,u)β(u)z, nonisotropic vectors span V in odd characteristic, forcing β=0. Leibniz makes B({u,v}_V,w) a completely alternating 3-tensor =tη, defining unique cross product C; the independent central alternating 2-form is uniquely η(u,v,w0). The Jacobiator is alternating 3-linear and vanishes on an orthogonal basis for both vector and central components; all (t,w0)∈K×V produce distinct brackets: q⁴. Associative automorphisms are Phi(u)=P u+f(u)z, Phi(z)=cz with P∈GO(B), P=sO since determinant²=c³ implies c square in odd q. For t≠0 scaling makes t=1 and f removes w0, one orbit. For t=0, w0 transforms by (det O)O ∈SO(B). SO3(q) is transitive on each nonzero quadratic-norm fiber, and nonzero isotropic vectors exist for every three-dimensional nondegenerate quadratic form over odd finite fields: central classes=0, nonzero isotropic, q−1 nonzero norms, q+1; total q+2. Independently checked all 81 t,w brackets over F3 on all 64 basis triples for Lie/Leibniz. Finite checks do not establish arbitrary odd prime powers/anisotropic form equivalence; algebraic proof does.
